key_facts: Council Bill 245 proposes a rezoning from Gmc's 32grx5 to General Urban Residential Mixed Use five story.
The rezoning requires an affirmative vote of ten to pass as there was a legal protest filed by the neighborhood.
The property is located in southeast Denver, along University Boulevard, in Council District six.
The property is approximately 75,000 square feet and is owned by no doubt Colorado, with a 7-Eleven at the corner of Wesley and University.
The proposed rezoning allows up to 70 feet in height, compared to the current allowance of 45 feet in the three story district.
The existing land use context includes commercial blocks zoned C-Max five to the west and G and U 12 to the south.
The planning board voted 9 to 0 to recommend support of the application on March 5th.
A petition of protest was filed by the neighborhood on May 5th and evaluated by CPD as a legal protest.
The rezoning is consistent with the University Park Neighborhood Plan and Blueprint Denver.
The proposed rezoning is consistent with the context and intent of the district and the neighborhood plan.
The rezoning is supported by the planning board and the developer, Tesla developments.
The neighborhood group, University Park Community Council, opposes the rezoning.
The rezoning is proposed to be placed upon final consideration and do pass.
The rezoning is expected to have a traffic impact of approximately 100 vehicles per hour during peak hours on Josephine and Harvard streets.
The developer has committed to working with the neighborhood on site access and traffic mitigation.
The rezoning was recommended by CPD based on the finding that all review criteria have been met.
The rezoning is part of the city's effort to encourage infill development and mixed-use projects along enhanced transit corridors.
The neighborhood has expressed concerns about increased traffic, loss of privacy, and impact on property values.
The developer has conducted a traffic study and solar study to address neighborhood concerns.
The rezoning is expected to result in a 236-unit residential building with 25,000 square feet of retail space.
